title: Apple Enters the Fray to Build Autonomous AI Agents? Job Listing Reveals Details, Possibly Launching as Early as End of Next Year

content_html:
As AI moves from passive Q&A to actively executing tasks, major tech giants are accelerating their efforts in the autonomous agent race. Apple is also developing autonomous AI agents capable of completing tasks on behalf of users, aiming to enter this high-growth market currently dominated by companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic PBC, and Meta Platforms Inc.

Job listings reveal core capabilities: coding, browsing the web, and controlling devices

Job listings posted on Apple’s website this week further confirm this trend. One listing shows that Apple is recruiting a senior engineering manager for a proactive, intelligent AI assistant. According to the job description, the system will be able to write code, browse the web, control applications, and directly operate devices on behalf of users.

The media reported earlier this month that Apple was developing an autonomous AI agent service, and these job listings provide more concrete evidence of that plan. However, the project is still in early R&D, and Apple plans to launch related services as early as the end of next year; Apple spokespeople declined to comment on the matter.

The agent race heats up: each player shows off its signature strengths

While Apple advances its related R&D, the AI agent market is already showing a highly active competitive landscape:

Meta and cross-device tools: Meta’s Muse recently made a breakthrough and drew widespread attention; it can help users book restaurants, arrange itineraries, and prepare news briefings. Meanwhile, many tools have also emerged on the market that allow AI to control Mac computers and write software programs.

Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google: Anthropic PBC recently expanded user testing for its Duet agent, while OpenAI expanded the capabilities of Dots; earlier this week, Google gave a comprehensive overhaul to its agent program, now called Tasks. In addition to standard AI agent capabilities, it also supports making phone calls on behalf of users, just like Elon Musk’s Grok Bot.

In Apple’s App Store, AI agent apps also hold an important place. Muse has long ranked No. 2 on the free app chart and on Thursday was behind only TikTok; OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Anthropic’s Claude also both made the top five.
